memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"They are to lay their hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place of the burnt offering. Then the priest is to take some of the blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar."'" - Lev 4:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ordinary Israelite lays his own hand on the head. Nobody does it for him.

Elders could represent the community. Nobody could represent this man. His own hand, on the head of his own goat, for his own sin.

There is a point at which faith cannot be delegated. Your parents' faith will not cover you. Your church membership will not cover you. Your family's reputation for godliness will not cover you. At some point, you must personally place your trust in Christ.

Ezekiel put it bluntly: the one who sins is the one who will die. The child will not share the guilt of the parent (Ezek 18:20). Every person stands before God individually.

That can sound frightening, but it is actually liberating. It means that no one else's failure disqualifies you, and no one else's faith is required to save you. The invitation comes to you directly.

Paul told the Philippian jailer: Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved (Acts 16:31). Not "join the right group." Believe.

Have you personally laid your hand on the head of the Lamb, or have you only stood nearby while others did?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I made my own personal commitment to Christ, or am I relying on someone else's faith?
2. What does it mean for me to trust Christ personally today, not just intellectually?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, I do not come to You on anyone else's account. I place my own trust in You today as my Saviour and substitute. Amen.
